newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli government settles Palestinian phone bill.
newsitem.headline: Israeli government settles Palestinian phone bill.

text.p: The Israeli government settled a 60 million shekel ($18.1 million) telephone bill owed by the Palestinian Authority, Bezeq Israel Telecom said on Monday.
"The Treasury will subtract the sum...from the money it is supposed to transfer to the PA and give it to Bezeq as soon as possible," Bezeq said in a statement.
Under an Israel-PLO economic accord, the Israeli government hands over to the self-rule administration in the West Bank and Gaza tax revenues collected from Palestinians working in the Jewish state.
Bezeq said it would now pay the Treasury 45.5 million shekels in fourth-quarter 1996 royalties that it had withheld pending settlement of the PA's bill.

The Authority has complained frequently of economic hardship stemming from Israeli closures of the West Bank and Gaza and delays in the dispatch of international donor money pledged to self-rule areas.
